# Independent review: oscillatory marginal hunt

Reviewed candidate: `REPORT_2026-09-15_OSCILLATORY_MARGINAL_HUNT.md`  
SHA256: `4d7b06b1a7e17eeb2822f282358772a929f362527209c5b98306cb8fe6840565`

## Verdict

**ACCEPT_SCOPED_THEOREM_MAPPING_AND_DIRECT_AFFINE_FILTERS_ONLY.**

Berndtsson's theorems concern Bergman-kernel diagonals or real positive
weighted integrals under plurisubharmonic/pseudoconvex hypotheses.  The
report correctly identifies that taking the modulus of the target Fourier
weight erases the unbounded oscillatory real spectral parameter; no
Bergman-diagonal identity or zero-free conclusion is supplied.

Barvinok's Gaussian and symmetric-exponential non-cancellation theorems have
the reported global Lipschitz and dependency budgets.  For both exact scalar
affine reweightings, the logarithmic derivative is unbounded in the Gaussian
case.  In the exponential case the reference-measure cusp gives a derivative
jump of two, hence Lipschitz constant at least one, contradicting the
`<=1/72` scalar budget.  The finite-splitting and `1/8` Gaussian argument is
also correct.

These results exclude only direct affine one-coordinate reweightings and
finite decompositions thereof.  Nonlinear transports, coupled
higher-dimensional lifts, other reference measures, and C6 beyond the
accepted central slab remain open; the report does not promote any of them.
